title: The closed subscheme cut out by a product of two ideal sheaves has the union as underlying set
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $i:Z\to X$, $i':Y\to X$ closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaves $\mathcal I_Z=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ and $\mathcal I_Y=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i'_*\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Then the product $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal I_Y$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$, there is a closed immersion $w:W\to X$ whose ideal sheaf $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to w_*\mathcal O_W)$ is $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal I_Y$, and its image is $w(W)=i(Z)\cup i'(Y)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), part (2): 'I_{Z cup Y} = I_Z . I_Y'; with Morphisms, Lemma 01QQ (morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-bijection-ideals, literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex) for the closed immersion of a quasi-coherent ideal, Schemes, Lemma 01IN (schemes-lemma-closed-subspace-scheme) for the affine-local description, and Algebra, Lemma 00E0 (algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology) part (9) with V(IJ) = V(I cap J) for the underlying set
